grammar_rules.summary: The infinitif présent can be used as the subject of a verb, corresponding to English gerund or present participle.
grammar_rules.explanation: In French, the infinitive is often used where English uses -ing form as subject.
usage: To express an action as the subject of a sentence.
grammar_rules.word_order: Infinitive at beginning of sentence as subject.
transformations: English gerund subject -> French infinitive subject
common_traps: Do not use present participle in French for subject; use infinitive.

attestations.source_text: The infinitif can be used as the subject of a verb. (Note that the present participle is used in English instead.)

grammar_rules.summary: The infinitive is used for general instructions, prescriptions, public notices, and proverbs.
grammar_rules.explanation: In French, the infinitive often replaces the imperative in formal or impersonal instructions.
restrictions: Modern household magazines tend to use imperative, but infinitive is used in professional contexts.
common_traps: Do not conjugate the infinitive; keep it invariant.

attestations.source_text: The infinitif is also used for general instructions, prescriptions, public notices, and proverbs

grammar_rules.summary: Negation ne...pas precedes the infinitive and is not separated.
grammar_rules.explanation: Because the infinitive is not conjugated, the negative elements are placed before the infinitive as a unit.
common_traps: Do not place ne before and pas after the infinitive.

attestations.source_text: the negation (ne… pas) does not surround the verb but rather precedes it, and is not separated.

grammar_rules.summary: Use infinitive after verbs of perception instead of English present participle.
grammar_rules.explanation: Verbs like voir, entendre, etc. are followed directly by infinitive.
usage: To express an action perceived by the subject.
transformations: English present participle after perception -> French infinitive
common_traps: Do not use the present participle in French.

attestations.source_text: The infinitive is used after verbs of perception (where the present participle is used in English).

grammar_rules.summary: Use question word + infinitive to form an interrogative infinitive.
grammar_rules.explanation: Interrogative words like que, comment, pourquoi, quoi are followed by infinitive.
usage: To ask a question in a concise way.

attestations.source_text: The infinitive is used in the interrogative infinitive.

grammar_rules.summary: Faire + infinitive expresses having something done or causing something to happen.
grammar_rules.explanation: The subject causes another person to perform the action.
transformations: English 'have something done' -> French faire + infinitive
common_traps: The object of faire may be placed before or after the infinitive depending on pronouns.

attestations.source_text: This causative form with faire is used to express the idea of having something done by someone or of causing something to happen.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Infinitive after expressions of spending time
grammar_rules.summary: After expressions like passer son temps à, gaspiller sa vie à, the infinitive is used with preposition à.
grammar_rules.explanation: The preposition à links the time expression to the infinitive.
usage: To describe how time is spent.
common_traps: Do not omit the preposition à.

attestations.section_title: Infinitive after expressions of spending time
attestations.source_text: The infinitive is used after expressions of spending time.

grammar_rules.summary: After expressions like être debout, être assis, the infinitive is preceded by à.
grammar_rules.explanation: The preposition à links the position expression to the infinitive.
usage: To describe an action done while in a certain position.

attestations.source_text: The infinitive is used after expressions of position. The preposition à precedes the infinitive.

grammar_rules.summary: Infinitif passé = avoir or être infinitive + past participle of main verb.
grammar_rules.explanation: For verbs conjugated with être in compound tenses, the past participle agrees with the subject.
conditions: Agreement of past participle with subject when using être.
agreement_rules: Past participle agrees with subject when auxiliary is être.

study.frequency_note: Common in written and formal French

attestations.source_text: It is formed with the infinitive of avoir or être and the past participle of the main verb. (Note that, for verbs conjugated with être, the past participle of the infinitif passé agrees with the subject of the sentence.)

grammar_rules.summary: Use après + infinitif passé to express an action completed before another.
grammar_rules.explanation: Après is followed by past infinitive, whereas avant de is followed by present infinitive.
usage: To indicate anteriority after another action.
common_traps: Do not use present infinitive after après.

attestations.section_title: après + past infinitive / avant de + present infinitive
attestations.source_text: One common occurrence of the infinitif passé is after the preposition après

grammar_rules.summary: Use avant de + infinitif présent to express an action occurring before another.
grammar_rules.explanation: Avant de is always followed by the present infinitive, not past.
usage: To indicate an action that happens before another.
common_traps: Do not use past infinitive after avant de.

attestations.section_title: après + past infinitive / avant de + present infinitive
attestations.source_text: the infinitif présent follows avant de

grammar_rules.summary: List of verbs not followed by a preposition before an infinitive.
grammar_rules.explanation: Certain French verbs are followed directly by an infinitive without any preposition. When the subjects of the two verbs differ, a que clause is used instead.
usage: After the listed verbs when the same subject performs both actions.
restrictions: Subject of first verb must be same as subject of infinitive; otherwise use que clause.
common_traps: Do not insert à or de after these verbs.

grammar_rules.summary: When the subject of the first verb and the infinitive differ, use que + subordinate clause.
grammar_rules.explanation: The dependent clause can be in indicative or subjunctive depending on the main verb.
usage: To express different subjects for two actions.
conditions: Subjunctive or indicative depends on main verb.
common_traps: Do not use infinitive when subjects differ.

attestations.source_text: When the subjects are different, a dependent clause introduced by que is required.

grammar_rules.rule_name: French verbs without preposition where English requires one
grammar_rules.summary: Some French verbs do not need a preposition even if their English equivalent does.
grammar_rules.explanation: Examples: attendre (wait for), abandonner (give up), écouter (listen to), entrer (walk in).
common_traps: Do not translate English preposition into French.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Negation with infinitive precedes it
exceptions_and_traps.description: With infinitive, negation ne...pas precedes the infinitive and is not separated.

attestations.source_text: the negation (ne… pas) does not surround the verb but rather precedes it, and is not separated.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Après requires past infinitive
exceptions_and_traps.description: Use past infinitive after après, not present infinitive.

attestations.section_title: après + past infinitive / avant de + present infinitive
attestations.source_text: One common occurrence of the infinitif passé is after the preposition après

exceptions_and_traps.title: Avant de requires present infinitive
exceptions_and_traps.description: Use present infinitive after avant de, not past infinitive.

attestations.section_title: après + past infinitive / avant de + present infinitive
attestations.source_text: the infinitif présent follows avant de

exceptions_and_traps.title: Some French verbs omit preposition even when English requires one
exceptions_and_traps.description: Verbs like attendre (wait for), abandonner (give up), écouter (listen to), entrer (walk in) do not take a preposition in French.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: attendre le train, écouter la conférence
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: attendre pour le train, écouter à la conférence

attestations.section_title: Verbs not followed by a preposition
attestations.source_text: In some cases, a French verb does not need a preposition even though its English equivalent requires one.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Use que clause when subjects differ
exceptions_and_traps.description: If the subject of the first verb and the infinitive differ, use que + subordinate clause instead of infinitive.

attestations.source_text: When the subjects are different, a dependent clause introduced by que is required.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Past participle agreement with être in past infinitive
exceptions_and_traps.description: For verbs conjugated with être, the past participle in the infinitif passé agrees with the subject.

attestations.source_text: for verbs conjugated with être, the past participle of the infinitif passé agrees with the subject of the sentence.
